notes: Shared case list for the bevy/ vgpu text comparison. Both sides read this file, so a case
cannot drift between them. Coordinates are top-left origin pixels; both renderers map them
into their own space. Colors are sRGB-authored RGBA with channels in [0, 1], decoded before
the vgpu side records them (see docs/text-reference.md). lineHeight is bevy's
`LineHeight::RelativeToFont` multiple. bounds is [width, height]; null leaves that axis
unbounded, and only the width feeds layout.
This is the published subset: one case per thing worth checking, each with a `notes` field
saying what it pins down. The full matrix that produced the numbers in docs/text-reference.md
also covered the other justify directions, the other two line-break strategies, 12/16/24 px
coverage and the remaining anchors; those were dropped as redundant, not as passing. Re-add
one by copying a neighbour and changing the field under test.

cases.notes: The block width counts the whitespace each line breaks at (bevy's `Layout::full_width`), and `Alignment` centres inside that box rather than inside the longest drawn line. Trimmed to the drawn glyphs, this case is off by half the trailing space.

cases.notes: Letter spacing lands after every character, the last one on the line included, because parley adds it to each cluster's advance. It therefore widens the block, not only the gaps.
A line holding a larger span gets a taller box — the run's own size drives the line height — and every span keeps its own colour.
`TextBounds.height` is not a layout input: the block runs past it instead of being truncated, matching bevy's `Text2d`. Three wrapped lines, all drawn.

cases.notes: Coverage baseline at a body-text size: the two rasterisers disagree by 1.4% of total ink, all of it on glyph edges.
The same string at a display size, where the edge band is proportionally wider and the rasterisers drift further apart (4.6% of ink, 1 px on the block width from float accumulation).
The anchor offsets by the rounded-up block size, not by the exact drawn extent, so a fractional block height moves the text by the ceiling.
The opposite anchor direction: the block is pulled up and left by its whole size, which checks the sign as well as the rounding.
